What was the likely cause of the surgically removed mass?

The mass at the base of the tongue is likely ectopic thyroid tissue due to failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland during embryonic development. This aligns with the consensus that such masses can occur when the thyroid does not descend properly. The reasoning chains that suggest 'failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland' are supported by the evidence of thyroid dysfunction related to the symptoms presented. Other options, such as maternal diabetes mellitus, radiation exposure, iodine deficiency, and failed fusion of the palatine shelves, do not directly correlate with the clinical presentation and are less likely causes of the mass.
